Started with a rough sketch of my idea
a compact device that will help me keep track of (not so) million dollar ideas, anytime anywhere. I also wanted to have a simple device that can serve as a to-do list without having to open my phone or laptop.

![rough look](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GnAePInLRlFkH5MpBRWBChfFoisaIEa2/55f6f9f37192f45180da84fdc44b6b367ec85b2c931714c36987318a387f91d7.png)

![3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GnAePInLRlFkH5MpBRWBChfFoisaIEa2/42bdbb1abf452f206afe554b3cab2045c96d7627b64fdfc76b352678fb2a3906.png)

Today, I created the first KiCad schematic for Notesy, adding the ESP32-S3, OLED, I2S microphone, microSD socket, three buttons, and USB-C connector. I assigned GPIOs and labelled the connections between the main components. I also added decoupling capacitors, the ESP32 enable circuit, and USB-C CC pull-down resistors. Running ERC helped me identify unconnected pins and power-related issues that still need resolving.
